title: ide-release
summary: Asks a running drag-lint Delphi IDE plugin not to respawn its drag-lint.exe child processes for a while -- and to drop the running one on its next request
intro: Read this when an engine build fails to copy drag-lint.exe because the Delphi IDE is open. ide-release writes a hold (--seconds N, 1 to 3600; 0, a negative number or no flag gives the default 120 s, and anything above 3600 is cut to 3600) so the plugin stops respawning the engine; --resume clears it and --status reports it. It frees nothing by itself.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint ide-release [--seconds N] [--resume] [--status] [--json] (writes a hold sentinel: a running Delphi IDE plugin will not respawn drag-lint.exe while it lasts and stops its LSP child on the next request that wants it, so the engine binary can be rebuilt while the IDE stays open; default 120s, --resume clears it early. Frees nothing by itself -- build\stage-engine.ps1 kills the running holder and retries. The plugin job queue also DEFERS its heavy jobs for the duration rather than starting them)
help: drag-lint ide-release [--seconds N] [--resume] [--status] [--json]   (writes a hold sentinel: a running Delphi IDE plugin will not respawn drag-lint.exe while it lasts and stops its LSP child on the next request that wants it, so the engine binary can be rebuilt while the IDE stays open; default 120s, --resume clears it early. Frees nothing by itself -- build\stage-engine.ps1 kills the running holder and retries. The plugin job queue also DEFERS its heavy jobs for the duration rather than starting them)

questions.ask: How do I rebuild drag-lint.exe while the IDE is open?
How do I cancel the hold early?
Is a hold active right now?
